extracted.intended_audience: registered patent and trademark practitioners (attorneys/agents) who practice before the USPTO; counsel and persons subject to USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, obligations, and sanctions under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and related procedural requirements for practitioners (patent and trademark) — including duties of competence, diligence, candor, supervision, account use, reporting, probation, and reinstatement conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of U.S. Licensed Attorney for Foreign Trademark Applicants (U.S. Counsel Rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark applicants not domiciled within the United States must be represented by an attorney who is licensed to practice law in a jurisdiction of the United States (37 C.F.R. § 2.11(a); Requirement of U.S. Licensed Attorney for Foreign Trademark Applicants and Registrants, Final Rule, effective August 3, 2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document notes the rule's effective date and that Respondent learned of the U.S. Counsel Rule before its effective date; failure to follow the rule supports a finding of incompetent representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent representation (37 C.F.R. § 11.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall provide competent representation to a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of failing to provide competent representation include not following § 11.18 (reasonable inquiry requirements), not following the U.S. Counsel Rule, failing to follow trademark rules for proper CAR signatory, and impermissibly signing oaths of inventorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failures include reviewing and signing declarations without a reasonable inquiry, not docketing and tracking Office Action deadlines, relying on foreign referring entities instead of communicating with clients, and forwarding Office Actions without follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor to a tribunal (37 C.F.R. § 11.303(a)-(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not knowingly make false statements of fact to a tribunal, must take reasonable remedial measures (including disclosure when necessary), duty of candor extends to the conclusion of the proceeding, and practitioner shall inform the tribunal of all material facts known to enable informed decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative misconduct: signing another person's signature on filings, not timely informing USPTO Trademark Operations of impermissibly signed filings, signing inventors' names to oaths knowing they did not sign, and failing to timely inform the Patent Office of impermissibly signed declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties regarding non-practitioner assistants (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.503(a) and (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall take reasonable efforts to ensure that a non-practitioner assistant's conduct is compatible with the professional obligations of the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing foreign referring entities access to USPTO.gov accounts and failing to supervise or monitor their activities (where they signed filings using the practitioner's credentials) violates these duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on assisting unauthorized practice of law (37 C.F.R. § 11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not assist another person in the unauthorized practice of law in a jurisdiction in violation of that jurisdiction's regulation of the legal profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Giving non-practitioners USPTO.gov accounts that they used to prepare/ file documents with the practitioner's credentials (resulting in unauthorized filings) constitutes assisting unauthorized practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dishonesty, fraud, deceit, misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include signing another person's signature to filings, signing declarations without conducting a reasonable inquiry (leading to misrepresentations about specimens), and signing inventors' names to oaths without due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct prejudicial to administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wide-ranging examples given: signing others' signatures, allowing non-practitioners to file using practitioner's credentials, failing to conduct reasonable inquiry before signing filings, signing inventors' names without diligence, and not timely informing the Office of impermissible declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable inquiry before signing trademark filings (37 C.F.R. § 11.18 referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must conduct an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances before signing declarations or other trademark-related filings that make factual attestations (e.g., specimens showing use in commerce).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists errors from cursory review: missing specimens; specimens not bona fide; specimens not reflecting the goods; signatures not matching designated signatories; misspellings; missing material information; and misinformation about representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized signatory requirements for Change of Address or Representation (CAR) forms
rubrics_metrics.description: A CAR form used to revoke a power of attorney for all previously appointed attorneys must be signed by the individual applicant/registrant or by a person authorized to legally bind a juristic applicant/registrant; it may not be signed by the original attorney of record or the new attorney of record when revoking powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent impermissibly signed numerous CAR forms to revoke existing powers of attorney, which is expressly disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper use and supervision of USPTO.gov accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners are responsible for how USPTO.gov accounts they open, sponsor, or provide access to are used and must supervise and monitor those accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented failures include opening/sponsoring accounts for foreign entities and employees, those entities filing using the practitioner's credentials (DIRECT method), IP addresses not matching the practitioner's firm, and the practitioner not reviewing filings before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and due diligence with foreign referring entities and clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must verify with referring entities and clients (where appropriate) facts necessary to truthful filings (e.g., whether applicants provided bona fide specimens) and must communicate with clients about Office Actions and Notices of Abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent relied on foreign referring entities without verification, did not confirm whether applicants had sent specimens, forwarded Office Actions and Notices of Abandonment without confirming client instructions, and assumed silence meant the client declined to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing and tracking deadlines for Office Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must maintain an adequate system to track deadlines for responses to Office Actions and not rely solely on third-party referring entities to communicate with clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's inadequate tracking (relying on referring entities) led to failures to follow up and potential abandonments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely notification to USPTO of impermissibly signed filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must timely inform USPTO Trademark Operations and the Patent Office when trademark or patent filings have been impermissibly signed or otherwise improperly filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent did not timely notify the USPTO of numerous impermissibly signed trademark filings and inventor oaths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature standards and use of ESIGN-ON/DIRECT methods
rubrics_metrics.description: When using ESIGN-ON or DIRECT signature methods, the practitioner must review filings and ensure signatures and attestations are proper before permitting or authorizing filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent used ESIGN-ON while spending inadequate time reviewing filings; Jinhua and One Stop used DIRECT to insert Respondent's signature and credentials on filings he did not review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on signing inventors' names to oaths without communication and due diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not sign inventors' names to oaths of inventorship unless the practitioner has communicated with the inventor and performed appropriate due diligence to verify accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent impermissibly signed approximately 450 inventor oaths, did not communicate with inventors prior to signing, did not engage in due diligence, and estimated the practice was to speed up filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with USPTO inquiries and disclosure obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must cooperate fully with USPTO inquiries into improper filings and disclose relevant account information and related details when ordered or agreed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent agreed to cooperate, to search for other USPTO.gov accounts, provide written lists (names/emails/addresses), and assist in present or future USPTO inquiries concerning improper filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions, limited recognition, and reinstatement procedures (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58, 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary sanctions (e.g., suspension), limited recognition to conclude pending matters, conditions for reinstatement, probationary periods, and restrictions on account use post-suspension are authorized under USPTO rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order: 16-month suspension from practice; 30-day limited recognition under §11.58(f) to conclude matters; prohibition after expiration from using/accessing/ sponsoring USPTO.gov accounts; requirement to petition for reinstatement under §11.60; and a 26-month probationary period after reinstatement is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing legal education requirements for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of reinstatement, practitioner must provide a sworn affidavit and evidence demonstrating completion of specified CLE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must complete 2 hours CLE on ethics, 2 hours CLE on law office management for solo/small practitioners, and 2 hours CLE on federal trademark law, and submit a sworn affidavit or verified declaration showing completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and reporting obligations during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: During probation, practitioner must regularly search USPTO systems and report findings to OED to identify filings listing the practitioner as attorney of record that were not made with the practitioner's knowledge or consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must monthly search TESS for applications identifying him as attorney of record and promptly notify USPTO in writing of filings not made by him; quarterly submit written reports confirming completion of searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to clients of suspension (methods for foreign clients)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner may provide written notice of suspension to foreign-domiciled clients by emailing a correctly translated copy of the Final Order to specified client email addresses, subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable recipients include the client's email in 'Applicant's Information' if it belongs to and is directly accessed by the client, or another client email reasonably believed to be directly accessed by the client; forwarding via foreign referring entities is allowed only if practitioner takes reasonable measures to ensure prompt forwarding and documents those measures in an affidavit for §11.58(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for and disclosure of other USPTO.gov accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must conduct a thorough search for any USPTO.gov accounts they opened, sponsored, had access to, or used in connection with trademark or patent matters and provide a written list including names, emails, and addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent ordered to conduct the search within 14 days and provide OED a written list; must continue to look for such accounts throughout probation and promptly report newly identified accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account dissociation, deactivation, and reactivation responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO may terminate/suspend/deactivate USPTO.gov accounts opened/sponsored/used by practitioner; reactivation is not automatic and is the practitioner's responsibility to arrange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon expiration of the 30-day limited recognition, USPTO authorized to deactivate listed accounts (and others); practitioner must contact appropriate USPTO business unit or acquire/create a new USPTO.gov account in accordance with policies to re-start or re-activate accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and enforcement procedures for probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED Director believes practitioner violated the Agreement, Final Order, or disciplinary rules during probation, OED may issue an Order to Show Cause and request immediate additional suspension up to eight months; procedural steps and response times are outlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order to Show Cause sent to practitioner's last address of record; practitioner granted 15 days to respond; OED may forward materials to USPTO Director requesting immediate suspension and may seek further discipline based on the same misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED electronic FOIA Reading Room and cause publication of a materially consistent notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, probation, underlying misconduct, and violated rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order includes a sample Official Gazette notice describing Respondent's suspension, probation, misconduct (trademark and patent examples), and the specific Rules of Professional Conduct violated.
